General Information:
Visa
As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visas on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
 Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).
Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $10,000 or its equivalent in gold (130g). For amounts exceeding up to $10,000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $20,000 in currency or gold is not permitted, Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find any stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are scarce in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD as the official rate. But usually, 100$ = 150000 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.

Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Head to Erbil.
Depending on the departure time we may have time to visit the Erbil Citadel and have a city tour of Erbil.

days.text:
Meet and greet. Transfer from the airport to the hotel.
A tour of the city of Basra can be arranged, depending on arrival time. This would include the following.
Visit the Museum of Basra, which used to be a presidential palace. (Usually closes at 1PM, but we can arrange entry at any time).
Visit old Basra canals and heritage houses of Al Ashar, it is famous for their unique architectural style, it is called Shanasheel.
Local food during the day, Basra is especially famous for its seafood meals.
Visit the corniche and have a tour with an Ashari boat at Shaat Al Arab. Also visiting the “Breeze Al Mansour” boat which was previously owned by the dictator Saddam.
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

Early morning drive to Al-Qurna, and see the meeting point of the Tigris and Euphrates as well as the biblical Tree of Knowledge.
We will then drive to Chibayish and have a marshland experience.
Have a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After lunch, drive to Nasiriyah.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

Note: We can optionally do an overnight stay in the Marshes, either camping or homestay with a local family.

Visit the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time.
Visiting the ancient city of Eridu, the first city in the world.
The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple.
After that, we will visit the UNESCO world heritage site, Uruk which is an ancient city of Sumer that played a leading role in the early urbanization. Writing may have originated in Uruk around 3300 BC. Evidence from excavations such as extensive pottery and the earliest known tablets of writing.
Head to Najaf.
Visit the “Valley of Peace”, the largest cemetery in the world.
We will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Overnight: Najaf / night 3

Head to visit the Grand Mosque of Kufa, and the house of Imam Ali.
We will head to Al-Kifl, a historic town that contains the tomb of the biblical Ezekiel.
Head to Karbala and check-in to the hotel.
Afterwards, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Overnight: Karbala / night 4

We will then drive to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
Visiting “Birs Nimrud”, and the Ziggurat of Borsippa.
After lunch, head to visit The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two metres.
Head back to Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
In the afternoon we can arrange for lunch or dinner with a local family.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

Have a morning tour of the monuments in Baghdad, including the Arabian Nights Monuments and save the culture monument.
Head to The Iraq Museum and wander in its galleries that will take us in a journey of civilizations of Iraq through the time.
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
Later head to the Modern part of Baghdad, to see the shopping centres and evening vibes of the city.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 7.

Head to Hit, and get to see the UNESCO world heritage site of the waterwheels on the euphrates.
After that we will go to the town of Fallujah passing by the famous prison of Abu Ghraib.
The traditional Kebab of Fallujah for lunch.
Head back to Baghdad
Overnight: Baghdad / night 8.

After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, Abu Dalaf mosque and minaret, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Afterwards we will head to Kirkuk and have a tour of the Citadel of the city.
Overnight: Kirkuk / night 9.

After breakfast, we will head to explore the site of Assur (Qal'at Sherqat), a UNESCO World Heritage site and the former capital of Assyria.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. 
We will see a breathtaking sunset from atop the temples of Hatra.
Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the towns.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 10.

AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in the evening.
Overnight: Mosul/ night 11.

Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban Hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
Head to Duhok and watch the sunset from on top of Zawa Mountain.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 12

After breakfast, head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Head to Jerwan and visit the first aqueduct in the world, a canal made by the assyrian empire.
Head to Khinis, and visit the origin of the canal with the assyrian reliefs.
Head back to Duhok.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 13

After breakfast, head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque. 
Head to Barzan, the city that stands as a testament to Kurdish resilience. The city where one of the most figure of Kurdistan’s politics was from (Mula Mustafa Barzani).  We will get to see the modern Barzani memorial that shows his interesting story amongst other important pieces.
Continue heading to Rezan, while enjoying the beautiful scenery on the way.
Overnight: Rezan / Night 14

After breakfast, head towards Soran. 
Soran, a city surrounded by mountains, where we will get to see the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.
Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and enjoying the view of the canyon.
See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering. 
Make a small stop in Shaqlawa for the buzzling markets in the city.
Head to Sulaymaniyah through the Dukan Lake Road.
Overnight: Sulaymaniyah / night 15.

Breakfast at the hotel.
Morning tour of Mawlawi’s market, where we will get to try some local restaurants and see its famous Langa (thrift) market.
Head back to Sulimaniyah and visit Amna Suraka, or the red museum, which documents some of the atrocities that were committed during the past regime’s time.
Start heading to Halabja, a village that suffered attacks from the past regime during the Iraq-Iraq war.
Back to Sulaymaniyah.
Overnight: Sulaymaniyah / night 16.

Head back to Erbil.
Depending on departure time, we can have a city tour of Erbil.
Transfer to Erbil Intl. Airport and Departure

End of tour

Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.

Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

The traditional Kebab of Fallujah for lunch.

Dinner of your choice.

days.text:
/ Monday, 20 January 
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

2884650-495299

/ Tuesday, 21 January  
Fast-Track visa and transfer, Arrival at 6 am.
After breakfast, start visiting the Museum of Basra.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar / Depending on the time.
Dinner would be the sea food of Basra!
Overnight: Basra / night 2.

/ Wednesday, 22 January    
4 AM start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive to Nasiriyah
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 3.

/ Thursday, 23 January  
Head to Eridu, an ancient sumerian city to the south of Nasiriyah,with it being probably the oldest city within the sumerian civilization.
Visiting the museum of Nasiriyah. 
Visiting the area of the Ziggurat.
After lunch, We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 4.

/ Friday, 24 January  
Head to Samawa and visit the UNESCO world heritage site, Uruk which is an ancient city of Sumer that played a leading role in the early urbanization. Writing may have originated in Uruk around 3300 BC. Evidence from excavations such as extensive pottery and the earliest known tablets of writing.
After that, head to Najaf and we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Visiting the largest cemetery in the world, Wadi Al-Salam ( Valley of Peace)
Overnight: Najaf/ Night 5.

/ Saturday, 25 January  
After breakfast, we will head to Karbala.
Visit Al-Ukhaidir Fortress, which represents Abbasid architectural innovation in the structures of its courtyards, residences, and mosque.
Lunch of your choice.
Afterwards, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Overnight: Karbala / night 6.

/ Sunday, 26 January    
7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
Time to visit two sites:
Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu.
Visiting the ancient city of Kish.
Head to Baghdad afterwards.
 Overnight: Baghdad / night 7.

/ Monday, 27 January    
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 8.

/ Tuesday, 28 January    
Have a morning tour of the monuments in Baghdad, including the Arabian Nights Monuments and save the culture monument.
Head to The Iraq Museum and wander in its galleries that will take us in a journey of civilizations of Iraq through the time.
Visiting The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two meters.In the afternoon head to the Modern part of Baghdad, to see the shopping centers and evening vibes of the city.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 9.

/ Wednesday, 29 January  
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Head to one of the most important ancient cities of Assyria, Ahsur, and visit the ziggurat of the city.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
 Overnight: Mosul / night 10

/ Thursday, 30 January  
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Visiting the gates of ancient nineveh.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 11.

/ Friday, 31 January  
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Head to Erbil.
 Overnight: Erbil / night 12.

/ Saturday, 01 February     
After breakfast, head towards Soran. 
Soran a city surrounded by mountains. In Soran we will get to see the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.
Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and enjoying the view of the canyon.
See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering. 
Make a small stop in Shaqlawa for the buzzling markets in the city.
Head back to Erbil. 
Overnight: Erbil / Night 13

/ Sunday, 02 February     
After breakfast, heading to the citadel to see the beautiful vibes from there, and explore the bazaar around it.
After lunch, visiting landmarks within the city, including Choli minaret and Khalil Jhayat Mosque.
Visiting the Syrian Heritage Museum.
Overnight: Erbil/ night 14.

/ Monday, 03 February 
Transfer to Erbil International Airport

General Information:
Visa
Iraq's (Visa on arrival scheme) started on the 15th of March 2021 which explain the following:
If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is:
(the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too.

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.  Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.

Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Najaf and check into the hotel that has a view of the Najaf Sea.
At night, we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Dinner of your choice.
Overnight: Najaf / night 3.

After breakfast, we will head to Karbala.
Visit Al-Ukhaidir Fortress, which represents Abbasid architectural innovation in the structures of its courtyards, residences, and mosque.
Lunch of your choice.
Afterwards, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Head Back to Baghdad
Overnight: Baghdad / night 4 .

8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 5 .

8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 6.

Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 7

Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head to Erbil and depending on time check in to the hotel and visit the citadel and the surrounding buzzling markets. 
Overnight: Erbil / Night 8

/ Sunday, 12 January  
Fast-Track visa & airport transfer to the hotel.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar / Depending on the time.
Dinner would be the sea food of Basra!
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

/ Monday, 13 January 
(1 15 hours) 4 AM Start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
(1 hr) We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
(1 30 hr) We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

/ Tuesday, 14 January  
(3 hours) Head to Najaf and we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Optional (Visit to Kufa).
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
(1 hour) We will then drive to Karbala
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
We will enjoy the energy of the city during the night, having local food, sweets and its famous Skanjabeel drink.
Overnight: Karbala / Night 3

/  Wednesday, 15 January  
(1 hour) 8:00 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site. 
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
(Undecided) We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
(1 hour) Head to Baghdad and Have lunch within the city.
Do a workshop of writing cuneiform on mud bricks with an expert.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad/ night 4.

/ Thursday, 16 January   
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
(0.45 hour) (Optional) Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
Head back to Baghdad to a Cultural Heritage cafe and enjoy a Baghdadi Chalghi concert/event.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

/ Friday, 17 January      
After Breakfast, heading to The Iraq Museum and wandering in its galleries will take us in a journey of civilizations of Iraq through the time.
Lunch as a Buffet or otherwise of your choosing.
Tour of Baghdad’s iconic monuments like the Martyr’s Monument and statues from the Arabian Nights.
At night we will head to the restaurant for Dinner.
(0.45 Hr)Time to visit The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two meters.
At night we will head to the restaurant for Dinner.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

/  Saturday, 18 January  
(2 hours) 7 30 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
(2 hours) After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
(1.30 hours) Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 7.

/  Sunday, 19 January  
8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

/ Monday, 20 January   
(1 hour) Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
For Departing Participants Head to Erbil for Departure
Optional Night in Erbil.
Kurdistan Extension

/ Monday, 20 January    
 (1 hour) Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
(1.30 hour) Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban Hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
(0.40 hour) Head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
(1 Hour) Head to Duhok
Overnight: Duhok / Night 9.

/  Tuesday, 21 January
After breakfast, Head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque. 
Head to Barzan, the city that stands as a testament to Kurdish resilience. The city where one of the most prominent figures of Kurdistan’s politics was from (Mula Mustafa Barzani).  We will get to see the modern Barzani memorial that shows his interesting story amongst other important pieces.
Enjoy the scenic route to Rezan.
Overnight: Rezan / Night 10.

/  Wednesday, 22 January  
After breakfast, head towards Soran.
Soran, a city surrounded by mountains. In Soran we will get to see the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.
Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and enjoying the view of the canyon
See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering.
Head to Erbil and make a tour of the Citadel’s Market
Departure to Erbil Int. Airport.
Overnight: Erbil / Night 11. (Optional)

Note: If you would like to pay cash, kindly make sure to bring 100$ notes or 50$ notes as they are most preferable to pay with in Iraq. However our team can receive any other smaller notes but it shouldn't be more than 30% of the total amount. Make sure that the 100$ Bills are printed after 2006 as older ones will not be accepted in all of Iraq.

General Information:
Visa
Iraq's (Visa on arrival scheme) started on the 15th of March 2021 which explain the following:
If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalise your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is:
(the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.  Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.

Contacts:
Don’t hesitate to contact us if you have any questions:
+9647804955885 l +9647904310853
book@bilweekend.com l www.bilweekend.com

Addresses:
Baghdad - Al Mansour - Amerat St. - Aamal Building / Office 308.
Baghdad - Al Karrada - The Station Coworking Space / Desk 70.

Registration:
Our registration code at The Iraqi Tourism Board of Tourism is 912 and the official name of our company is Rehlat Al-Utla Travel Co.

Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.

We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.

8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will go to the town of Fallujah passing by the famous prison of Abu Ghraib.
The traditional Kebab of Fallujah for lunch.
Back to Baghdad, to visit The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two meters.

7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
Time to visit two sites:
Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu.
The tomb of Ezekiel. This site is special due to its shared history and importance for both Muslim and Jewish devotees.

You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).

It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.

/ Friday, 10 January
Fast-Track visa & airport transfer to the hotel.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar / Depending on the time.
Dinner would be the sea food of Basra!
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

/ Saturday, 11 January     
4 AM Start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

/ Sunday, 12 January     
Head to Najaf and we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Optional (Visit to Kufa).
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Karbala
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
We will enjoy the energy of the city during the night, having local food, sweets and its famous Skanjabeel drink.
Overnight: Karbala / Night 3

/ Monday, 13 January

Head to Baghdad and Have lunch within the city.
Do a workshop of writing cuneiform on mud bricks with an expert.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad/ night 4.

/ Tuesday, 14 January  
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
(Optional) Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
Head back to Baghdad to a Cultural Heritage cafe and enjoy a Baghdadi Chalghi concert/event.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

/ Wednesday, 15 January     
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 6.

/ Thursday, 16 January     
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 7.

/ Friday, 17 January     
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
For Departing Participants Head to Erbil for Departure
Optional Night in Erbil.

Kurdistan Extension

/ Friday, 17 January    
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban Hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
Head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 8.

/ Saturday, 18 January     
After breakfast, Head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque. 
Head to Barzan, the city that stands as a testament to Kurdish resilience. The city where one of the most prominent figures of Kurdistan’s politics was from (Mula Mustafa Barzani).  We will get to see the modern Barzani memorial that shows his interesting story amongst other important pieces.
Enjoy the scenic route to Rezan.
Overnight: Rezan / Night 9.

/ Sunday, 19 January    
After breakfast, head towards Soran.
Soran, a city surrounded by mountains. In Soran we will get to see the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.
Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and enjoying the view of the canyon
See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering.
Head to Erbil and make a tour of the Citadel’s Market
Departure to Erbil Int. Airport.
Overnight: Erbil / Night 10. (Optional)

(the Israel entity)

Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Dinner of your choice.

, Tuesday, 24th March
Meet and greet, and fast track visa from the airport to the hotel. (Night 1)
Introductory tour of Baghdad’s landmarks: This will include statues from the Arabian nights & others like Abu Nuwas St. and Al Firdous Square.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires. (40 KM) (0.75 Hour Drive)
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

, Wednesday, 25th March
 7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School 
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an
explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
Iraqi Masgouf for dinner.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 3.

Thursday, 26th March
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.  (130 KM) (1.5 Hour Drive)
Back to Baghdad, to visit The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. (180 KM) (2 Hour Drive)
The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two metres.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 4.

Friday, 27th March
In the morning, head to the Iraq Museum, and explore its national treasures.
After lunch, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.  (90 KM) (1 Hour Drive)
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
Head back to Baghdad, and explore the modern parts of the city.   (90 KM) (1 Hour Drive)
We can do a pottery making / cuneiform writing workshop.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

Saturday, 28th March
Transfer to Baghdad Intl. Airport and departure.
End of tour

After breakfast, Head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque.

After that head to Khinnis, where assyrian reliefs can be seen and observe what used to be a quarry for the empire.
Head to Mosul and check-in to the hotel.

Head back to Mosul for lunch
Visiting the site of Nineveh, starting with the gate of Adad going through the main Palace area and visiting the library of Ashurbanipal.
Visiting Jonas Hill
Have dinner in the city.

General Information:
Visa
Iraq's (Visa on arrival scheme) started on the 15th of March 2021 which explain the following:
If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Covid-19
All tours are open for bookings. Iraq is no longer asking for PCR tests or making extra checks on vaccination for both entry or departure from 1 December 2022.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is:
(the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveller is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit. As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visas on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
 Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).
Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalise your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.  Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.

days.text:
, Oct 23, Thursday
Arrival at Basra Intl. Airport (Pickup according to selection)
After breakfast, Head to the museum of Basra that once was one of the old presidential palaces in Basra.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Overnight: Basra / Night 1

, Oct 24, Friday
4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive back to Nasiriyah.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

, Oct 25, Saturday
We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Head to Najaf and we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Overnight: Najaf / Night 3

, Oct 26, Sunday
After breakfast, we will head to Karbala.
7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
Lunch of your choice.
Afterwards, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Overnight: Karbala / night 5.

, Oct 27, Monday
After breakfast, Start Heading to Baghdad.
By 9 30 AM, visiting the Iraq Museum and getting to explore its galleries.
Lunch in the city.
After lunch, Start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
 Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

, Oct 28, Tuesday
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
Head to lunch, and have a free afternoon/evening in Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6

, Oct 29, Wednesday
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

, Oct 30, Thursday
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

, Oct 31, Friday
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head to Erbil.
End Of Tour

General Information:
Visa
Iraq's (Visa on arrival scheme) started on the 15th of March 2021 which explain the following:
If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.
Others:(Malaysia & Singapore) Added in May 2024.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Covid-19
All tours are open for bookings. Iraq is no longer asking for PCR tests or making extra checks on vaccination for both entry or departure from 1 December 2022.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is:
(the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.  Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.

230 V, 50 Hz

(the Israel entity)
