Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. Drop off in Mosul.

/ Sunday, 30 March  Day 1 of Eid (OBSERVED)
Arrival from Airport, transfer to hotel & Checkin -  Night 1.
Visiting the museum of Basra, which was once one of the old governmental palaces. (May be closed due to Eid)
Checkin in the hotel.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra. Followed by a trip on the Italian Bridge.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar / Depending on the time.
Visiting the Armenian Church.
Dinner would be the sea food of Basra!
Overnight: Basra / night 2.

/ Monday, 31 March  Day 2 of Eid (OBSERVED)
5 AM Start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the mud house with a local family.
Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
 After lunch, we will drive to Nasiriyah.
Overnight: Nasiriyah/ night 3.

/ Tuesday, 01 April   Day 3 of Eid (OBSERVED)
After breakfast, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Najaf and make a visit to Kufa.
At night, we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Visiting “The Valley of Peace” the largest graveyard in the world.
Dinner of your choice.
Overnight: Najaf / night 4.

/ Wednesday, 02 April     Day 4 of Eid (OBSERVED)
8 AM After breakfast, start heading to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site. 
Head to Birs Nimrud, a sister city of Babylon, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Lunch of your choice.
Head to Karbala.
After hotel check-in, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Overnight: Karbala / night 5.

/ Thursday, 03 April
7 AM Start Heading to Baghdad.
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and Abbasid Palace.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch, visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
After that, head to Baghdad & check-in.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

/ Friday, 04 April
After Breakfast, heading to The Iraq Museum and wander in its galleries that will take us in a journey of civilizations of Iraq through the time.
Lunch as a Buffet or otherwise of your choosing.
Tour of Baghdad’s iconic monuments like the Martyr’s Monument and statues from the Arabian Nights.
At night we will head to Zamzam Restaurant for Dinner.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 7.

/ Saturday, 05 April
7 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra.
9:30 AM arriving in Samarra, visiting the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
By 1 PM Have lunch on the way.
By 2 PM, Head out to Hatra.
By 3:30 PM arrive to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

/ Sunday, 06 April
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 9.

/ Monday, 07 April
8 AM Visit Bahzani village where we can have breakfast with a local family at their house, followed by a visit to local factories of alcohol, sesame oil.
Start heading to the Monastery of Rabban Hormizd in Al-Qosh. 
Afterwards, heading to Lalish, arguably the holiest place for Yazidi faith and learning about the Yazidis, their history and religion.
Head to Duhok and check- in into the hotel.
Have some time to explore the city.
Overnight: Duhok/ night 10.

/ Tuesday, 08 April
After breakfast, start heading to Amedi, arriving at noon, a town on the top of a mountain that rises1000 metres high. We will get to explore this unique town that has been there for thousands of years.
Lunch at Amedi.
Heading to Barzan and enjoying the nature within the village and learning about its history.
Visiting the memorials of Barzan.
Afterwards heading to Serzan and checkin to Rubar Resort
Overnight: Serzan/ night 11.

/ Wednesday, 09 April
After breakfast, start heading to Shanidar cave that once held the skeletons of 120,000 years old Neanderthals
After that we will head to Rawanduz, an area that has a long history and very interesting stories from World War One.  Then head to see the beautiful nature of Bekhal waterfall and Geli Ali Beg.
Head to Erbil with a possible stop at Shaqlawa to visit the market.
Check-in to the hotel.
Overnight: Erbil/ night 12.

/ Thursday, 10 April
After Breakfast head to the citadel to see the buzzling markets there, and explore the bazaar around it.
Visiting the beautiful Jalil Khayat mosque.
Visiting the Syriac Heritage museum.
Having free time to explore the city
Overnight: Erbil/ night 13.

/ Friday, 11 April
Transfer to Erbil Int. Airport

End of Tour

7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favourites. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
Head to visit The Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of fifty-two metres.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

, Sunday Mar 15
7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Najaf, to visit the shrine of Imam Ali as well as “The Valley of Peace”, the largest cemetery in the world.
We will then drive to Karbala and check-in to the hotel.
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
We will enjoy the energy of the city during the night, having local food, sweets and its famous Skanjabeel drink.
Overnight: Karbala / night 3.

, Monday Mar 16
We will drive to Nasiriyah
After lunch, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time.
The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Free time at night to enjoy dinner or a cafe.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 4.

, Tuesday Mar 17
4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the mud house with a local family.
Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After lunch, drive back to Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5

, Wednesday Mar 18
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 6.

, Thursday Mar 19
8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 7.

, Friday Mar 20
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh for breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land. 
Afterwards head to Akre, and witness the Nowruz celebrations and the famous fire ceremony.
An option to join celebratory walks with the locals.
Head to Erbil
Overnight: Erbil / night 8.

, Saturday Mar 21
After breakfast,Head to Rawanduz, and enjoy the area’s beautiful landscapes and canyons. Visit Bekhal and Gali Ali Beg waterfall, as well as Korek Mountain Resort.
Head back to Erbil, where we will have some time to explore the city’s nightlife.
Overnight: Erbil / night 9.

, Sunday Mar 22
Head Back to Erbil and Transfer to Erbil International Airport.
End of tour

General Information:
Visa
As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visa on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
 Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).
Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $10,000 or its equivalent in gold (130g). For amounts exceeding up to $10,000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $20,000 in currency or gold is not permitted, Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find any stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are scarce in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD as the official rate. But usually, 100$ = 150000 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.

7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Visit the UNESCO world heritage site, Uruk which is an ancient city of Sumer that played a leading role in the early urbanization. Writing may have originated in Uruk around 3300 BC. Evidence from excavations such as extensive pottery and the earliest known tablets of writing.
After that head to Nasiriyah
Have dinner at Nasiriyah. 
Overnight: Nasiriyah / Night 1

4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After lunch.
We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
After that, drive back to Baghdad.

 3* $900

8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 1.

8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.

Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.

Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.

As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visa on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.

 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).

(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).

(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor.

Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $10,000 or its equivalent in gold (130g). For amounts exceeding up to $10,000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $20,000 in currency or gold is not permitted, Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find any stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are scarce in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD as the official rate. But usually, 100$ = 150000 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.

Traditional dinner of your choice.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 1.

8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 2.

/ Wednesday, 23 April     
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 3.

/ Thursday, 24 April    
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
Head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 4.

/ Friday, 25 April     
After breakfast, Head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque. 
Head to Barzan, the city that stands as a testament to Kurdish resilience. The city where one of the most figure of Kurdistan’s politics was from (Mula Mustafa Barzani).  We will get to see the modern Barzani memorial that shows his interesting story amongst other important pieces.
Continue heading to Soran, while enjoying the beautiful scenery on the way.
Overnight: Soran / Night 5

/ Saturday, 26 April  
After Breakfast, explore Soran.
A city surrounded by mountains. In Soran we will get to see the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.
Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and enjoying the view of the canyon.
See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering.
Head to Halabja a city that faced a genocide by the former regime yet is still there and thriving, we will get to see it’s local markets and the famous memorial.
Later in the evening, visit Salim’s street. A street bustling with local food carts and shops. 
Overnight: Sulimaniyah / Night 6

/ Sunday, 27 April  
After breakfast, have a Morning tour of Mawlawi’s market, where we will get to try some local restaurants and see its famous Langa (thrift) market.
visit Amna Suraka, or the red museum, which documents some of the atrocities that were committed during the past regime’s time.
Start heading to Erbil. 
Depending on time check in to the hotel and visit the citadel and the surrounding buzzling markets. 
Dinner in Erbil.
Overnight: Erbil / Night 7

Departure from Erbil Int. Airport

days.text:
/ Sunday, 15 December  
Meet and greet, and fast track visa  from the airport to the hotel. A tour of Baghdad’s landmarks can be arranged if arriving time before sunset.
This will include statues from the Arabian nights & iconic monuments.
Traditional dinner of your choice.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 1.

/ Monday, 16 December  
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the Abbasid Palace.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

/ Tuesday, 17 December  
7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Karbala
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
We will enjoy the energy of the city during the night, having local food, sweets and its famous Skanjabeel drink.
Overnight: Karbala / night 3.

/ Wednesday, 18 December  
Head to Najaf.
Head to the Grand Mosque of Kufa, one of the earliest mosques in Islam. Also visit the house of Imam Ali.
Visit the “Valley of Peace”, the world’s largest cemetery, before checking into the hotel.
At night, we will visit the shrine of Imam Ali, and tour the Najaf Grand Bazaar.
Overnight: Najaf / night 4.

/ Thursday, 19 December
We will drive to Nasiriyah
 After lunch, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. 
The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. 
We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets. 
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 5.

/ Friday, 20 December     
4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive back to Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

/ Saturday, 21 December     
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 7.

/ Sunday, 22 December
8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

/ Monday, 23 December 
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum.
Visit the astonishing Monastery of Rabban hormizd that is located on top of a mountain. 
head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Overnight: Duhok / Night 9.

/ Tuesday, 24 December   
After breakfast, head to Amedi, a historical town on top of a mountain engulfed by beautiful scenery. Where we will see a number of historical sites like the ancient gates and the Amedi’s great mosque. 
Head to Barzan, the city that stands as a testament to Kurdish resilience. The city where one of the most figure of Kurdistan’s politics was from (Mula Mustafa Barzani).  We will get to see the modern Barzani memorial that shows his interesting story amongst other important pieces.
Overnight: Barzan / Night 10.

/ Wednesday, 25 December 
After breakfast, continue heading to Soran, while enjoying the beautiful scenery on the way.
Head to Erbil and depending on time check in to the hotel and visit the citadel and the surrounding buzzling markets. 
Departure to Erbil International Airport.

Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.

Local breakfast in the mud house with a local family.
Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
 After lunch, we will drive to Nasiriyah.
Overnight: Nasiriyah/ night 3.

/

The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Najaf and check into the hotel that has a view of the Najaf Sea.
At night, we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Visiting “The Valley of Peace” the largest graveyard in the world.
Dinner of your choice.
Overnight: Najaf / night 4.

/  
Start the day visiting Kufa, which holds one of the earliest mosques in Islamic history and the place of the death of Imam Ali.
Lunch of your choice in Karbala.
After hotel check-in, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Overnight: Karbala / night 5.

/

We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Lunch of your choice.
Time to visit two sites:
Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu.

Lunch of your Choice
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
After that, head to Baghdad & check-in.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

/

Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School.

At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 7.

/

By 1 PM Have lunch on the way.
By 2 PM, Head out to Hatra.

/

Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 9.

/

Lunch of your choice.
Having an open double decker bus tour of the city by sunset with having free time afterwards.
Overnight: Mosul/ night 10.

Head to Duhok and check- in into the hotel.
Have some time to explore the city.

Heading to Barzan and enjoying the nature within the village and learning about its history.
Visiting the memorials of Barzan.
Afterwards heading to Serzan and checkin to Rubar Resort

Check-in to the hotel.

Visiting the beautiful Jalil Khayat mosque.
Visiting the Syriac Heritage museum.
Having free time to explore the city
Overnight: Erbil/ night 14.

If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).

(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.
Others:(Malaysia & Singapore) Added in May 2024.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Covid-19
All tours are open for bookings. Iraq is no longer asking for PCR tests or making extra checks on vaccination for both entry or departure from 1 December 2022.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is:
(the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.  Follow the weather forecast to know more about what you should wear and bring with you.

General Information:
Visa
As of March 1, 2025, Iraq is no longer issuing visa on arrival. All travellers must now apply for an eVisa prior to their arrival in Iraq. If you are from one of the below countries, your eVisa will be issued within 24 hours of your application. We can also apply on your behalf for a lower fee than the official government rate.
The list of the countries:
Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway and Hong Kong).
Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman).

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.
Connections are available to destinations worldwide via other regional airlines such as Turkish Airlines, Qatar Airways, Emirates, Royal Jordanian and many others. Our transfer has been pre-arranged within the package. No need to buy a mobile sim card from the airport, as our logistical team will help you do this in the city.
Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $10,000 or its equivalent in gold (130g). For amounts exceeding up to $10,000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $20,000 in currency or gold is not permitted, Please note that this limit is calculated per person traveling.

Money
You will find it tough to find any stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are scarce in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Currency information
Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD as the official rate. But usually, 100$ = 150000 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit.

General Information:
Visa
Iraq's (Visa on arrival scheme) started on the 15th of March 2021 which explain the following:
If you are from these 40 countries you can get the visa sticker at the airports (Baghdad Airport, Basra Airport and Najaf Airport) and also by land at the borders (Between Iraq and Jordan - West of Iraq region, Between Iraq and Kuwait - Entry to Iraq through Basra, Between Iraq and Iran – Entry to Iraq through Basra).
The list of the countries:
 Permanent members of the Security Council:
(UK, USA, France, Russia, China).
 EU Countries:
(Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark, Ireland, Gibraltar, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Sweden, Austria, Finland, Estonia, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia).
Countries with strong economic ties with Iraq:
(Australia, Canada, South Korea, Japan) Also (New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Singapore) added later.
 Gulf Council of Cooperation Countries:
(Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman) added later in December 2022.

e-Visa
Iraq's (e-Visa Portal) started on the 15th of February 2024. This will make the visa application process as easy and hassle-free as possible:
All citizens of other nationalities don't need to visit an Iraqi embassy or Iraqi consulate anymore! All you need is a valid passport and personal photo of yourself and finalize your trip details with us. We will take care of everything else for  you.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Passport
You will need your passport in all Iraqi checkpoints and hotels. Make sure you have at least six months valid on your passport on your arrival date, an empty page in your passport for the Iraqi visa sticker, otherwise you might have some issues at the border. 
Make sure you have no stamp on your passport from regions that have no recognition from Iraq, The region is: (the Israel entity)

Airport
There are five international airports in Iraq.
The main one is Baghdad International Airport which is located 16km away from downtown Baghdad. It is the country's largest air hub, and home base for the national airline (Iraqi Airways) where passengers can take its flights within Iraq such as Baghdad - Erbil or Basra and also you can travel to some regional destinations.

Most of our itineraries start in Baghdad and end in Erbil or Basra. Just double check with us before booking your flight. 
Currency and Gold Carrying Limit 
Each traveller is allowed to carry up to $5000 or its equivalent in gold (130g) without declaration. For amounts exceeding $5000 up to $10000, declaration at customs is required. Carrying more than $10000 in currency or gold is not permitted. Please note that this limit is calculated per person travelling.

Money
You will find it tough to find many stores that will accept cards. Your best would be bringing all the cash you will need for your trip with you beforehand. ATMs are available but not common in Iraq, and occasionally the servers will go down, so it won’t be possible to withdraw any money. Bringing USD will not be a big problem as it is also accepted and exchanged and most preferable notes are (100$ and 50$) issued in the year of 2006 and after.

Iraqi Dinar (IQD; symbol ID). In use notes are in denominations of IQD (50,000 - 25,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 - 1,000 - 500 - 250).
1$ = 1320 IQD is the official rate. But usually, 1$ = 1500 IQD in daily use in the market.

Tips
It is up to you to ask for a hand to help you out. If someone is asking to help you and you do not need it, just say no thank you!
In case you accepted the help then your tips in hotels or airports should not be more than 5,000 IQD.
It is always welcomed to tip more if you are happy or liked the service of the person.
To tip our staff, just use the same tradition that you do in your country. Iraq is your home too!

Clothing
It is always wise to dress respectfully. You should not stress too much about what to wear, but as a general rule of thumb, especially for women, you should try and cover as much of your shoulders and knees as you can. Long pants and loose-fitting t-shirts. Ideally, skirts should cover your ankles but covering just your knees would be fine too.
In holy shrines, men are not allowed to wear shorts and women should wear scarves and Abaya and our female team will help you wear the suitable dressing for that, do not worry at all - you all are welcomed to visit. / Monday, 8 December
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School.
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
After lunch start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad

/ Tuesday, 9 December
7:30 AM After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Karbala
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
We will enjoy the energy of the city during the night, having local food, sweets and its famous Skanjabeel drink.
Overnight: Karbala / night 1.

/ Wednesday, 10 December 
We will drive to Nasiriyah
 After lunch, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

/ Thursday, 11 December     
4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive back to Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad

/ Friday, 12 December
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 3.

/ Saturday, 13 December  
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 4.

/ Sunday, 14 December     
Early morning head to the Plains of Nineveh. Have breakfast with a local Christian family in Bahzani and learn their stories and history.
Visit some of the Yazidi temples in the town.
Head to Erbil to visit the citadel and the surrounding buzzling markets. 
Head Back to Baghdad

Passport

Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.

Head back to Baghdad

Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 4.

/ Sunday, 20 April     
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.

The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.

head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their most holy and important land.
Head to Erbil.

Head to Sulaymaniyah

Head back to Sulimaniyah and visit Amna Suraka, or the red museum, which documents some of the atrocities that were committed during the past regime’s time.

Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz
We advise you to bring a universal electricity adaptor. 

Covid-19
All tours are open for bookings. Iraq is no longer asking for PCR tests or making extra checks on vaccination for both entry or departure from 1 December 2022.

Passport

(the Israel entity)

/  Wednesday, 12 March
After breakfast, start visiting the Museum of Basra.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar / Depending on the time.
Dinner would be the sea food of Basra!
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

/ Thursday, 13 March     
Start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After  lunch, start heading to Qurna, the point meeting of Tigris and Euphrates rivers, also exploring the Tree of Adam - An ancient jujube tree of Knowledge mentioned in the Bible.
We will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Head to Najaf and we will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Overnight: Najaf / Night 2

Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.
We will then drive to Karbala
At night, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Head  to Baghdad
Overnight: Baghdad / night 3.

/ Saturday, 15 March

Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.
At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 4.

/ Sunday, 16 March     
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 5.

/ Monday, 17 March     
 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 6.

/ Tuesday, 18 March     
Drop off in Erbil or Transfer to Erbil International airport.
End of tour

We will drive to Nasiriyah

The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. We also can witness one of the most beautiful sunsets.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive through Basra with a possible stop at the corniche of Shatt Al Arab and head back to Safwan with drop-off.
End of Tour

/ Saturday, Oct 4
Arrival in Basra airport in the morning and transfer to the hotel.

Having a walk in old Basra with Shanasheel houses, Ashar Canal and the Old Basra Bazar.
Visit the Hassun Museum and Pasha Aian Library.
Lunch at Shanasheel Restaurant.
River tour in Shatt Al Arab by Ashari boats and have a walk in the Cornish of Basra.
Overnight: Basra / night 1.

/ Sunday, Oct 5
Early morning we will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.
Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After that, drive to Nasiriyah
After lunch, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time. 
The site includes Abraham house, Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple.
Head to Najaf.
Overnight: Najaf / night 2.

/ Monday, Oct 6
Visit the “Valley of Peace”, the world’s largest cemetery.
Optional: We will walk to the area of the shrine of Imam Ali and will have the chance to visit the grand bazaar of Najaf.
Head to Al-Kifl and visit Ezekiel’s tomb.
Then we will head to Karbala and visit Al-Ukhaidir Fortress, which represents Abbasid architectural innovation in the structures of its courtyards, residences, and mosque.
Optional: Visiting Al-Aqaise Church, the oldest church in Iraq.
Then we will head to Karbala and have some time exploring the modern part of the city in the evening.
Overnight: Karbala / night 3.

/ Tuesday, Oct 7
After breakfast we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.
Then we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage site.
We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, the place where Alexander the Great passed away.
We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces that was built during the past regime time with special access to the upper floors.
Head to Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu.
Head to Baghdad afterwards.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 4.

/ Wednesday, Oct 8
7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer and Kahi).
Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”.
Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School, the Abbasid Palace, and the Baghdadi Museum
This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi.
Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or any other of your favorite. We also will grab a treat from both Al Shahbender cafe  and Haj Zbala Juice shop.
Visit the grave of Gertrude Bell.
Optional: Visit the Martyr’s Monument.
Then start heading to Salman Pak:
Visiting Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5.

/ Thursday, Oct 9
Visit the Ziggurat of Dur-Kurigalzu and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about fifty-two meters.
Visit one of: The Gallery, the Fine Art Society, or the National Museum of Modern Art depending on exhibitions at the time.
Visit the Royal Cemetery and the shrine of Kadhimiya.
Optional: We can do a cuneiform writing workshop on this day.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 6.

/ Friday, Oct 10
8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Head to visit Assur, a UNESCO World Heritage site and the first capital of Assyria.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
 Overnight: Mosul / night 7.

/ Saturday, Oct 11
After breakfast head to the archeological site of Nimrud (Kalḫu), one of the Assyrian capitals.
After that we will head to head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. 
Overnight: Mosul / night 8.

8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
Visiting the gates of ancient nineveh and Nabi Yunus Mosque.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 9.

Head towards Al-Qosh, a Christian town that is home to the tomb of prophet Nahum and the Rabban Hormizd Monastery.

Visit the Khinis Reliefs and the Jerwan Aqueduct.
Head to Erbil.
 Overnight: Erbil / night 10.

After breakfast, visit the Erbil Citadel and the citadel’s Bazaar.
Visit other landmarks like Choli Minaret and Jalil Khayat Mosque.
Visiting the Syrian Heritage Museum.
Then head to Akre and have a walk around the Old Town with views of the city from Sare Gri (Top of the Hill).
Enjoy a traditional Kurdish dinner with some local desserts.
Head back to Erbil. 
Overnight: Erbil / Night 11.

Transfer to Erbil International Airport

End of Tour

At night we will have free time for dinner, café or drink.

Lunch of your choice.
Afterwards, we will walk to the area between the two shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas, with more explanation about the battle of Karbala in the tour.

We will drive to Nasiriyah
After lunch, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time.

Free time at night to enjoy dinner or a cafe.
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 4

4 AM We will drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland experience.
Local breakfast in the mud house with a local family.
 Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world and a UNESCO world heritage site.
After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the reed house - Al Mudhif.
Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on the water over the centuries.
After sunset, drive back to Baghdad.
Overnight: Baghdad / night 5

8 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious center with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.
Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm Baajeen) for dinner.
Overnight: Mosul / night 6

8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church that are being rebuilt by UNESCO.
Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle against ISIS took place.
Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.
The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal made by locals.
See the remains of ancient Nineveh and the last of its gates.
Free time in Mosul and at night visiting the cafe house for local music performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the battles.
Overnight: Mosul / night 7

7 AM visit Bashiqa, a Yazidi/Christian town. Where you can have the unique experience of meeting with the locals, having breakfast prepared by an Iraqi Christian family and get to hear their stories
Head to Lalish and have a unique experience with the Yazidis in their holiest land.
Finally head to Erbil
Overnight: Erbil / night 8

The hike will be for 6-8 hours total, depending on fitness level.
You may choose to do one of multiple easier hikes in the area.
Head back to Erbil.
Depending on arrival time, we may have a city tour of Erbil.
Overnight: Erbil / night 9

Transfer to Erbil Intl. Airport.
